extracted.intended_audience: educators, NEA members, students, and policymakers concerned with Title IX enforcement
extracted.subtask_description: A union-issued press statement responding to a U.S. Department of Education action that rescinds or rolls back negotiated Title IX resolution agreements; argues for enforcement and protections for students, including trans and LGBTQ students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schools must be safe, inclusive places
rubrics_metrics.description: "We owe it to every student to ensure schools are safe, inclusive places where they can learn and thrive."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEA frames a primary evaluative standard as student safety and inclusivity: policies and enforcement actions should prioritize environments where students can learn without fear of bias or harassment. Rollbacks that undermine safety or inclusion are unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforce Title IX protections against sexual harassment and discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: "Title IX’s protections against sexual harassment and discrimination" must be enforced rather than abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR and the Department of Education should actively resolve cases of sexual harassment and assault in K–12 and higher education; failing to resolve cases constitutes abdication of responsibility (the release notes OCR did not resolve a single K–12 sexual harassment/assault case last year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rescind previously negotiated resolution agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Affirmative rescission of provisions of previously negotiated resolution agreements undermines commitments made with schools to address findings of gender discrimination under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement treats reversal of closed Title IX matters as highly unusual and a departure from longstanding enforcement practices; such reversals are framed as harmful precedent that weakens protections for students and should be opposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX covers broad areas of education participation and protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX "covers everything from athletics to admissions to protection from harassment and violence."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating compliance or policy changes, assess impacts across these substantive domains (athletics, admissions, harassment/violence protections) rather than narrowly limiting coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections must include gender identity and sexual orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Title IX guarantees that all students, regardless of sex—including their gender identity or sexual orientation—can learn in safe, welcoming environments."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies or enforcement practices should explicitly protect transgender and LGBTQ students; singling out these students or excluding them from protections is contrary to NEA's interpretation of Title IX and harms student safety and equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy actions should strengthen, not weaken, protections for vulnerable students
rubrics_metrics.description: At a time when protections should be strengthened for our most vulnerable students, some politicians are choosing to divide communities and make schools less safe by singling out certain students for who they are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposed policies or rollbacks by their effect on vulnerable populations; actions that single out groups or reduce protections are flagged as unacceptable and politically motivated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longstanding enforcement practices should be maintained
rubrics_metrics.description: Reversals of closed Title IX matters "are highly unusual and represent a significant departure from longstanding enforcement practices."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames continuity with historical enforcement as a criterion: departures from precedent warrant scrutiny and are taken as indicators of harmful policy shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR effectiveness metric: resolution of sexual harassment/assault cases
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR's performance is measured by whether it resolves cases of sexual harassment or assault in K–12 schools (the release notes OCR did not resolve a single such case last year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should track case resolutions as an outcome metric for agency commitment to Title IX enforcement; lack of resolutions is presented as evidence of abdication.
